_metadata.independence: I read only u24-blind-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or API was consulted.

hints.reason: Arctic ice is immediate, but nothing recognizable links the Arctic to pirates.
Rum is the pirate's drink; the ice side rests on 'rum on ice' / a rum cocktail, which is reachable but secondary.

best_available.why: Pirate side is instant and 'rum on ice' is a real drinking phrase, so a player can land both; ARCTIC never reaches pirate.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair is hard: ice and pirate share no obvious scene; RUM is the only hint that touches both.

hints.reason: Bling is flashy jewellery (rings), and 'ice' is the slang word for diamonds within the same bling vocabulary.
Ice rink is direct, but a rink is not a ring to a player; the etymological link is invisible.
A diamond ring is the archetypal ring, and 'ice' is the well-known slang for diamonds.

best_available.why: Both sides are broad and sit in the same jewellery scene.

pairs.pair_note: Two good jewellery-route hints; RINK is a false friend.

hints.reason: Ice is cold physically; a robot is 'cold' emotionally, a familiar shared-property stretch like RICH for BANK+KING.
Frozen is ice; a robot 'freezes' when it seizes up (or the robot dance freeze), a thinner route than COLD.

best_available.why: Cold-and-unfeeling is a standard way to describe robots, so the shared property is recognizable.

pairs.pair_note: Only the shared-property route exists; COLD carries it, FROZEN is a weaker variant.

hints.reason: Rock-hard is idiomatic and ice is a hard solid; a defensible shared property.
'On the rocks' means on ice, but the hint contains the target ROCK, which is a rule failure.
Whiskey on ice and whiskey on the rocks are the same familiar bar order.
A glacier is ice; glaciers grind and carry rock (moraine), which a player may or may not reach.

best_available.why: One ordinary drink order points at both words.

pairs.pair_note: WHISKEY is excellent; ROCKS would be ideal but is disqualified by containing the target.

hints.reason: Frozen is ice; there is no familiar frozen-rose scene or phrase to reach rose.
Frost is ice; frost on rose petals (and frost killing roses) is a real garden image but not a strong pull toward rose specifically.
Ice sculpture is familiar; roses are a common sculpture subject but a player would more likely name a swan.

best_available.why: A frosted rose is a recognizable image, giving the only two-way route offered.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; every hint is anchored on the ice side with a weak reach to rose.

hints.reason: Winter brings ice, and salting the roads is a winter chore; a shared seasonal scene.
Salt melts ice; the two words meet in one everyday action.
Road salt is spread to clear icy roads; the same scene as MELT viewed from the road.

best_available.why: Salt melting ice is the direct, universally known interaction.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; all three hints share the winter-road scene.

hints.reason: Shade is a near-synonym of shadow and has no recognizable route to ice.
Ice is cold; it is colder in the shadows, a real but secondary association for shadow.

best_available.why: Shadows being cold is a lived experience, so a player can reach both, though shadow is not a strong pull.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; COLD is serviceable, SHADE is pure filler toward one side.

hints.reason: Shark fin is immediate; there is no fin route to ice.
Greenland is the ice sheet; the Greenland shark is a real, moderately known species (famous for its age).

best_available.why: Both facts are true and the shark side is reachable by a reasonably informed player.

pairs.pair_note: GREENLAND is the only two-way hint and leans on a moderately niche animal fact.

hints.reason: Only works via 'cold-blooded' to snake; 'blooded' alone does not reach ice.
Ice is cold; snakes are the archetypal cold-blooded animal, a familiar shared property.

best_available.why: Cold-blooded is the standard snake descriptor and ice is cold.

pairs.pair_note: COLD does the job; BLOODED is a fragment that only works if you already know the answer.

hints.reason: Spider web is immediate; nothing links web to ice.
Frost is ice; a frosted web is a photo cliche but it points at web, not spider.

best_available.why: Weak either way; frost on a spider's web is at least a real image, whereas WEB has zero ice side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS and no genuine two-way hint; the pair likely needs a new idea (e.g. a creature or brand that spans both).

hints.reason: Ice melts and the spring melt is a familiar seasonal phrase.
Ice thaws; 'spring thaw' is a set phrase.
River-ice breakup as a spring season is real but regional (northern Canada/Alaska); most players will think of relationships.

best_available.why: 'Spring thaw' is a set phrase and thaw implies ice.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; BREAKUP is a regional term (flagged british_only in the sense of regional usage, not UK).

hints.reason: Stars twinkle (nursery rhyme); ice sparkles or glitters rather than twinkles, so the ice side is a stretch.
Ice skater is immediate; star via a figure-skating star or 'Stars on Ice' is reachable but secondary.
Ice crystal is a set phrase; crystal reaches star only via star-shaped snow crystals or crystal star ornaments.

best_available.why: Ice is instant and the skating-star / 'Stars on Ice' association gives the most recognizable second step.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; every hint is anchored on one side with a soft reach to the other.

hints.reason: Snowpiercer is a train that circles a frozen Earth; one story reaches both words for anyone who knows it.
Polar ice is direct; train comes via The Polar Express, a familiar compound.
Express train is direct; ice only via Polar Express (or Germany's ICE InterCity Express), both second-order.

best_available.why: Broader than Snowpiercer and the Polar Express is widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Two usable story/brand routes; EXPRESS is the weaker half of the same compound.

hints.reason: Ice cube is immediate; water only as the thing the cube is made of or dropped into, a weak pull toward water itself.
Ice is frozen water; the hint names the exact relationship.
Ice melts into water; the reverse of FROZEN and equally direct.

best_available.why: 'Frozen water' is literally the definition of ice.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair with two ideal hints.

hints.reason: Elsa's ice powers are universally known; she is a queen/sorceress rather than a witch, so the witch side needs a hop.
The White Witch of Narnia rules an icy world, but 'white' alone reaches ice only as a colour and witch only via that one character.
Narnia under the White Witch is frozen in eternal winter; one familiar story carries both words.

best_available.why: The frozen land and its witch are the two things everyone remembers about the story.

pairs.pair_note: NARNIA is the clean story route; ELSA is nearly as good if the owner accepts 'ice witch' as a fair label for her.

hints.reason: Tundra is frozen ground and wolves are its signature predator; a shared habitat.
Arctic ice is direct and the Arctic wolf is a well-known animal.
Winter brings ice; wolves howling in a winter forest is a stock scene.

best_available.why: Arctic wolf is a named animal and Arctic ice is immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Solid geography/habitat pair.

hints.reason: Lock and key is instant; iron only via old iron locks, which is a weak pull toward iron.
Blacksmith works iron and a locksmith cuts keys; one word, two familiar compounds.

best_available.why: Both compounds are everyday words.

pairs.pair_note: SMITH is an elegant compound route; LOCK is one-sided in practice.

hints.reason: 'Iron fist' is a set phrase; a king ruling with a fist is reachable only after the iron step.
The Man in the Iron Mask is the king's secret twin; the story links both, though the king side needs the plot.
The Iron Throne (Game of Thrones) and a king's throne.

best_available.why: Iron Throne is one of the best-known modern compounds and throne means king.

pairs.pair_note: THRONE is excellent; MASK is a fair story route.

hints.reason: Knights carry swords and swords are forged from iron/steel; a shared scene.
A knight in iron armor; both words sit in one image.
Iron Man is direct; knight via 'a man in armor' or Iron Man as a modern knight is a stretch.

best_available.why: Suit of iron armor is the knight image.

pairs.pair_note: Strong medieval scene; MAN is the weak one.

hints.reason: Iron and the lion are both standard emblems of strength; a shared property like RICH for BANK+KING.
Iron gate is direct; lion via stone lions flanking gates or the Lion Gate is a secondary image.
A circus or zoo lion behind iron bars in a cage is one familiar scene.

best_available.why: Iron cage and caged lion share a single picture.

pairs.pair_note: Two usable hints; GATE is iron-weighted.

hints.reason: Earth's iron core is broad; the moon's small core is a specialist fact and 'core' does not pull toward moon.
Iron Man and the Man in the Moon are both familiar compounds.
Iron meteorites and the moon's meteor craters are both true, but neither side is the first thing a player reaches from meteor.

best_available.why: Two everyday phrases, no explanation needed.

pairs.pair_note: MAN carries the pair; the astronomy hints are plausible but soft.

hints.reason: Iron cage and a pet mouse's cage; a shared object.
Mousetrap is immediate; iron via heavy iron traps (bear traps) is reachable but not a strong pull.

best_available.why: Both are cage animals/materials in one picture.

pairs.pair_note: CAGE is fine; TRAP is mouse-weighted.

hints.reason: Iron gate is direct; there is no recognizable gate route to night.
Iron Curtain is a set phrase; 'the curtain of night' is poetic and only a soft pull toward night.

best_available.why: Only hint with any reach to night (nightfall as a curtain), and the iron side is strong.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the pair needs a new idea (e.g. something that spans knight/night wordplay would not count, so a shared scene is required).

hints.reason: Iron rusts; salty ocean air and water are the classic cause of rust.
The Titanic sank in the ocean and was a great iron (steel) ship; the story reaches both.
Ocean is direct; iron only via the rusting iron hull of a wreck, a secondary image.
An iron anchor dropped in the ocean; one object, both words.

best_available.why: Anchors are the iconic iron object of the sea.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair; SHIPWRECK duplicates TITANIC with a weaker iron side.

hints.reason: Captain Hook's iron hook; the pirate's prosthetic is literally iron.
Pirate ships fire iron cannon; shared object.
Iron chains are direct; pirates in chains (captured, hanged) is a reachable but secondary image.

best_available.why: The pirate hook is a named iron object.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair with two clean object routes.

hints.reason: Queen Cersei sits the Iron Throne; the story reaches both for Game of Thrones viewers.
The Iron Lady is a famous epithet; a queen is the first lady of a realm, a fair rank route.
Iron Throne and a queen's throne.

best_available.why: Broadest and most direct on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Three passes; CERSEI is the most fandom-dependent.

hints.reason: An anvil is iron and an anvil rings when struck; verb sense of ring is allowed.
Iron rusts; 'ring rust' (boxing) is too niche to count as a ring route.
Iron is forged, and the One Ring was forged (Lord of the Rings); forging a ring is familiar.

best_available.why: Forging iron and forging a ring are both common phrases.

pairs.pair_note: FORGE and ANVIL work; RUST is one-sided.

hints.reason: Iron is a metal; robots are metal; a shared material that is central to both.
The Iron Giant is a robot; one film title carries both words.
Iron Man is direct; robot via 'mechanical man' or the suit being robotic is a hop.

best_available.why: Immediate on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair; MAN is iron-weighted.

hints.reason: A meteorite is a rock from space and iron meteorites are the famous kind.
Magnets attract iron; rock only via magnetite/lodestone, a specialist step.
Iron ore is rock containing iron; the compound names both.

best_available.why: Iron ore is the everyday compound and ore is rock.

pairs.pair_note: ORE is ideal; MAGNET is the weak one.

hints.reason: Rose garden is direct; iron only via wrought-iron garden gates and furniture, a soft pull.
Iron Maiden is a set name; no recognizable maiden route reaches rose.
Iron gate is direct; roses climbing a gate is a picture but not a strong rose pull.

best_available.why: The wrought-iron gate in a rose garden is the one scene that holds both, and rose garden is instant.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the pair's only shared scene is a wrought-iron rose garden, which neither hint nails.

hints.reason: Iron and salt are both minerals, including on a nutrition label; a shared category.
Sea salt is direct; sea has no recognizable iron route.
Iron rusts and salt is the famous accelerator of rust (salted roads, sea air).

best_available.why: Both words are textbook minerals.

pairs.pair_note: Two passes; SEA is filler toward salt only.

hints.reason: Iron bar is direct; nothing recognizable links bar to shadow.
Iron Curtain is a set phrase; a curtain casting shadow or the Cold War's 'shadow' is an invented rescue.

best_available.why: Weak either way; a curtain at least darkens a room, whereas BAR has nothing on the shadow side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS and no genuine two-way hint; the pair needs a fresh idea.

hints.reason: Jaws is the shark film; 'jaws of iron' or iron-jawed as a grip metaphor is a soft iron route.
Shark-cage diving puts a diver in a metal (iron) cage; one scene, both words.

best_available.why: Shark cage is a known compound and cages are iron.

pairs.pair_note: CAGE carries the pair; JAWS is shark-weighted.

hints.reason: Iron rod is direct; snake via the rod of Asclepius or Moses' staff is a learned step.
A snake coils; iron coil only via coiled iron/electromagnet cores, a soft pull.
Iron pipe is direct; a plumber snakes a pipe with a drain snake, a familiar verb/tool use.

best_available.why: Iron pipe plus the plumbing snake gives a genuine two-way route.

pairs.pair_note: PIPE is a neat route; the others are one-sided in practice.

hints.reason: Iron Man is a founding Avenger and Spider-Man joins the team in the films.
Iron Man and Spider-Man; two of the best-known compounds in popular culture.
Both heroes are Marvel characters.

best_available.why: Both compounds are instant.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair via the superhero route.

hints.reason: Spring mattress is direct; iron bed frames are not an iron route a player would take from mattress.
Coil spring is direct; iron coil is a soft pull toward iron.
Steel is made from iron, and springs are steel; a shared material.

best_available.why: Steel sits between the two words naturally.

pairs.pair_note: STEEL carries the pair; the rest are spring-weighted.

hints.reason: Iron core (Earth) is broad; a star's core is a familiar notion and stars fuse up to iron in their cores.
Iron Man is direct; star via Starman or 'star of the film' is a stretch.
A meteor is a shooting star, and iron meteorites are the famous kind.

best_available.why: Shooting star is instant and iron meteorite is well known.

pairs.pair_note: METEOR is the clean route; CORE passes on the strength of 'core' being a word used of both planets and stars.

hints.reason: Train tracks are iron rails.
'Iron horse' is the classic nickname for a train; one phrase names both.
Iron rails carry trains.

best_available.why: A single idiom that means both.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; TRACKS and RAILS are near-duplicates.

hints.reason: A steam iron is an everyday appliance and steam is boiled water.
Iron pipes carry water.
Iron plus water makes rust; the two words are the recipe.

best_available.why: Steam iron is a named compound and steam is water.

pairs.pair_note: Very strong pair.

hints.reason: Horseshoes are iron; nailing one over the door to keep witches out is classic folklore, though not everyone knows the witch part.
Iron as a ward against witches is folklore lore; 'ward' alone pulls weakly toward either word.
The witch's cauldron is a cast-iron pot; one object, both words.

best_available.why: Cast-iron cauldron is the witch's signature prop.

pairs.pair_note: CAULDRON is ideal; HORSESHOE is a fair folklore route, WARD is too thin.
